_: بيان (Bayan) — the Pulse glossary. One Arabic term per concept, decided once. Rationale lives in BAYAN.md. Enforced by `npm run lint:ar`.

concepts.note: Genitive/accusative inflection (العملاء المحتملين) is correct Arabic after a مضاف — the linter checks vocabulary, never case.
Never المراقبة — that is surveillance, the exact connotation our ORG-only guardrail exists to reject.

banned.why: Transliterated English. A product that writes Arabic this way reads as translated, not authored.
Transliteration of a platform nickname; the Arabic names the function.
A physical line of people. A publishing queue is قائمة.
Surveillance. Wrong register and wrong ethics for market listening.
Bureaucratic passive. Marketing register addresses the reader directly: «تُرسل الحملة» or «أرسِل الحملة», not «يتم إرسال الحملة».
Padding calqued from English 'perform/do'. «أنشئ حملة», not «قم بإنشاء حملة».
Petitionary register. Software instructs politely by being direct.

bannedPunctuation.why: English plural hack. Arabic has six plural categories — use the plural helper.

structural.allowLatinNote: Latin is allowed in three cases only: (1) industry acronyms Arabic marketers say in Latin, (2) proper nouns, (3) literal strings the user must type or match exactly — CSV headers, template variables, env vars, URL fragments. Anything else is untranslated text and fails. Single Latin letters are allowed as path/grade/version markers (/f/, grade A, v2, Q1).
